impact.argument: Retain the exact native deterministic hidden-K model, feasible publicz0, monotone beta-LipschitzF, exact arbitrary-direction LMO with every legal fixed tie rule, and atom-hull query/output restriction. The SAME algorithm queries g=F(z0), then s=LMO(g), and outputs this atom s, with all initialization included, exact pathwise budget(1,1). For everyu inK, <F(u),s-u>=<g,s-u>+<F(u)-g,s-u><=beta||u-z0||||s-u||<=beta DK². Thus on the closed coarse predicate epsilon>=beta DK² this single output succeeds deterministically for everyinstance and every tie rule. Necessity of bothcoordinates is the exact accepted proof_necessary: on K=[-DK/2,DK/2]e1 and z0=0, constant fields+Me1 and-Me1 are monotone and beta-Lipschitz for arbitraryM. Without anyFcall, same public inputs/K/LMO map imply an identical deterministic transcript/output. The average of their weakgaps is M DK/2, so M>2epsilon/DK contradicts a uniform guarantee: BF>=1. Without anLMOcall, every permissible output lies in the initial hull{z0}, regardless ofFqueries. Field+Me1 then has weakgapM DK/2>epsilon, so BLMO>=1. Separate adversarial instances suffice because a single advertised cap must work for allinstances. No bounded-operator-norm assumption limitsM, and no free projection or evaluated hidden-domain output is allowed. Hence everyattainable pair has BF>=1,BLMO>=1, while the same(1,1) algorithm establishes everypair aboveit. The exact attainable region is therefore{BF>=1,BLMO>=1}; no splicing of scalar optimizers or a scalar ratio is involved. The extra simplex inequality in oldb_necessary is compatible and redundant here: R=beta DK²/epsilon<=1 gives RHS=1/(d+1)+8/R>=8 while1/(BLMO+1)<=1/2 forBLMO>=1. The threshold is sufficient, not proved sharp or the largest(1,1)region. Fine-accuracy operator/Pareto rates and fullc1 remain unclosed. This is publication of a previously proved consequence, not a new paper result or extension outside the original fullD.

proofs.proof: Write D=D_K, eta=1/beta, C=D^2, delta=epsilon/(4beta), R=beta D^2/epsilon. To approximately minimize q(w)=eta<g,w>+||w-x||^2/2 over K, initialize s0=LMO(g). Since s0 minimizes the linear term, H0=q(s0)-min q<=C/2 and its FW gap G0=max_v<eta g+s0-x,s0-v><=C. Thus no bound on ||g|| is required. Quadratic smoothness gives q(s+alpha(v-s))<=q(s)-alpha G(s)+C alpha^2/2, where v=LMO(eta g+s-x). If delta>=C return s0. Otherwise run m=ceil(8C/delta) FW updates with alpha_j=2/(j+2), j=0,...,m-1. Convexity gives G>=H; induction in the preceding descent inequality yields H_m<=2C/(m+2)<delta/4. Now test G using one LMO per test. If G>delta, update with alpha=delta/C. Each failure reduces q by strictly more than delta^2/(2C). Consequently one of n=ceil(C/(2delta)) tests must succeed, since n failures would reduce q by at least delta/4, contradicting H_m<delta/4. Each prox therefore costs at most Q=1+ceil(32R)+ceil(2R) LMO calls; it uses no new F calls. All updates are convex combinations of already feasible points and returned atoms. Use x1=z0; for t=1,...,T=ceil(R), query F(xt), compute yt with this prox at center xt, query F(yt), and compute x(t+1) with the same center and g=F(yt). A successful gap test gives <eta g+w-x,w-u><=delta for every u in K. The two inequalities, the identity for squared distances and eta beta=1 give eta<F(yt),yt-u><=(||xt-u||^2-||x(t+1)-u||^2)/2+2delta: the remaining cross term eta<F(yt)-F(xt),yt-x(t+1)> is absorbed by (||yt-xt||^2+||yt-x(t+1)||^2)/2. This is also Theorem 3.1 in the read source. Sum over t and use monotonicity <F(u),yt-u><=<F(yt),yt-u>. The average ybar has Minty gap <=beta D^2/(2T)+2beta delta<=epsilon. Costs on every execution path are at most (2T,2TQ), including initialization, with all F queries and output in the permitted atom hull. Linear minimizers need not be vertices or unique; every legal tie choice satisfies the proof.
proofs.statement: Uniform full-LMO specialization and explicit query caps.

proofs.proof: Query g=F(z0), then s=LMO(g), and output s. For every u in K, <F(u),s-u>=<g,s-u>+<F(u)-g,s-u><=beta||u-z0||||s-u||<=beta D_K^2, because <g,s-u><=0 by exact linear minimization. This holds for all legal fixed tie choices, and output s is an allowed atom. Thus epsilon>=beta D_K^2 admits budget (1,1). Combined with the independently proved necessary B_F,B_LMO>=1, this determines the entire attainable budget region on this sufficient coarse region. The threshold is an exact sufficient algorithm threshold; no assertion of its sharpness is made.

When d=1, compact convex K is a closed interval, possibly a point, and monotonicity means F is nondecreasing. Query F(z0). If it is zero, z0 has zero Minty gap. Otherwise call LMO(F(z0)); the unique relevant endpoint a is the left endpoint when F(z0)>0 and the right endpoint when F(z0)<0. Query F(a). If F(a) has the same weak sign as F(z0), output a, which solves the VI exactly. Otherwise a and z0 bracket signs. Write the ordered bracket [l,r] with F(l)<=0<=F(r). Repeatedly query its midpoint and retain a sign bracket (stop if the value is zero). After k=max(0,ceil(log2(beta D_K^2/epsilon)/2)) queries the bracket length h<=D_K/2^k. Output its midpoint z. For u outside [l,r], monotonicity gives F(u)(z-u)<=0. Inside, the endpoint signs and Lipschitz property give |F(u)|<=beta h and |z-u|<=h, so F(u)(z-u)<=beta h^2<=epsilon. Every queried point and the output is a convex combination of z0 and the sole returned atom. Costs are at most (2+k,1), including initialization. On epsilon<beta D_K^2, this dominates the main construction: for R>1, (log2 R)/2<=R-1, hence k<=ceil(R)-1 and 2+k<=2ceil(R); its LMO allowance is also smaller. On epsilon>=beta D_K^2 the one-pair upper bound dominates this cap.

First, use K=[-D_K/2,D_K/2]e1 in R^d and public z0=0, with identical public enclosing ball and identical legal LMO rule. Constant fields F=+M e1 and F=-M e1 are monotone and beta-Lipschitz for every M. Without an F query, the deterministic transcript and output are identical on these two instances. At least one weak gap is >=M D_K/2, so M>2epsilon/D_K rules out every cap B_F<1. Without an LMO call, the allowed output hull is {z0}; the constant field +M e1 then has gap M D_K/2 irrespective of F queries, ruling out B_LMO<1. Thus no uniform zero-query region exists at any finite positive epsilon. For the rate-dependent constraint, let K be a regular d-simplex in R^d with d+1 centered vertices v_i of side D_K, public z0=v_1, and F(x)=beta x. It is an admissible monotone beta-Lipschitz instance. Choose a legal deterministic LMO rule that returns a minimizing vertex, with fixed index tie-breaking; target correctness must cover this rule. After m LMO calls, the output z is supported on at most m+1 vertices. The Gram matrix has <v_i,v_j>=(D_K^2/2)(1_{i=j}-1/(d+1)), so for z=sum lambda_i v_i, ||z||^2=(D_K^2/2)(sum lambda_i^2-1/(d+1))>=(D_K^2/2)(1/(m+1)-1/(d+1)). Here sum lambda_i=1, lambda_i>=0, and Cauchy-Schwarz on the support proves sum lambda_i^2>=1/(m+1). The inequality remains valid, though possibly trivial, when m>=d. Since 0 in K and u=z/2 in K, Minty gap >=<beta z/2,z/2>=beta||z||^2/4. Consequently epsilon accuracy requires 1/(m+1)<=1/(d+1)+8epsilon/(beta D_K^2). Since m<=B_LMO, the stated necessary budget inequality follows. Operator queries cannot evade the hull support constraint; there are no additional target assumptions. This constructs a subclass of the original target preserving queries, output restriction, deterministic guarantee and both cost coordinates. The bound is meaningful up to the finite-dimensional support scale d, not a theorem of exact reconstruction or uniform saturation at d calls.

proofs.body: Retain the exact native deterministic hidden-K model, feasible publicz0, monotone beta-LipschitzF, exact arbitrary-direction LMO with every legal fixed tie rule, and atom-hull query/output restriction. The SAME algorithm queries g=F(z0), then s=LMO(g), and outputs this atom s, with all initialization included, exact pathwise budget(1,1). For everyu inK, <F(u),s-u>=<g,s-u>+<F(u)-g,s-u><=beta||u-z0||||s-u||<=beta DK². Thus on the closed coarse predicate epsilon>=beta DK² this single output succeeds deterministically for everyinstance and every tie rule. Necessity of bothcoordinates is the exact accepted proof_necessary: on K=[-DK/2,DK/2]e1 and z0=0, constant fields+Me1 and-Me1 are monotone and beta-Lipschitz for arbitraryM. Without anyFcall, same public inputs/K/LMO map imply an identical deterministic transcript/output. The average of their weakgaps is M DK/2, so M>2epsilon/DK contradicts a uniform guarantee: BF>=1. Without anLMOcall, every permissible output lies in the initial hull{z0}, regardless ofFqueries. Field+Me1 then has weakgapM DK/2>epsilon, so BLMO>=1. Separate adversarial instances suffice because a single advertised cap must work for allinstances. No bounded-operator-norm assumption limitsM, and no free projection or evaluated hidden-domain output is allowed. Hence everyattainable pair has BF>=1,BLMO>=1, while the same(1,1) algorithm establishes everypair aboveit. The exact attainable region is therefore{BF>=1,BLMO>=1}; no splicing of scalar optimizers or a scalar ratio is involved. The extra simplex inequality in oldb_necessary is compatible and redundant here: R=beta DK²/epsilon<=1 gives RHS=1/(d+1)+8/R>=8 while1/(BLMO+1)<=1/2 forBLMO>=1. The threshold is sufficient, not proved sharp or the largest(1,1)region. Fine-accuracy operator/Pareto rates and fullc1 remain unclosed. This is publication of a previously proved consequence, not a new paper result or extension outside the original fullD.
